items.summary: Databricks announced new Databricks Genie plugins that give teams a governed interface to enterprise context in ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot Cowork and Grok Bot. The company says agents often guess through an organization's data because they lack business meaning; the announcement introduces Genie Ontology as a layer combining governed definitions with continuously learned organizational knowledge so agents can interpret terms like certified activation metrics or revenue shortfalls. Plugins let agents retrieve context, run SQL and return cited answers, route specialized questions to domain-specific Genie Agents, and continue work themselves when needed. The company notes the plugins are available today in those four clients.
items.title: Databricks Unveils Genie Plugins for AI Agents

items.summary: IBM says it will deliver IBM Quantum Starling, a fault-tolerant quantum computer slated for 2029 that can run about 100 million hard operations on 200 qubits. The company reports progress across six areas: validated c-coupler technology and improved qLDPC codes reducing required connections from six to five; a Relay-BP decoder meeting Starling requirements; modular l-couplers linking processors with improving repeatability; rectangular modular cryogenics wiring up to 3.84 miles of trace length per bay, with two Nighthawk r2 devices already cooling as of November 2026; and cryogenic ASIC control electronics matching room-temperature performance. IBM notes the architecture is unchanged but Starling remains years away.
items.title: IBM Outlines Pathway to Fault-Tolerant Quantum Starling

items.summary: A New York Times report alleges that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy plot involving Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, which supplies chips to Nvidia. US intelligence reportedly warned officials she may have been a Ministry of State Security asset, while China denies any involvement and calls the claims slander. Trump denied prior knowledge during a Monday press conference. The scandal has shaken Nvidia’s stock, which rose about 600 percent over five years but fell sharply in recent weeks. Questions remain about whether top administration officials were briefed.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Caught in Chinese Spy Allegations Amid Trump Ties

items.summary: In a blog post dated 11th November 2026, the author introduces Anthropic's IPO roadshow video, which contains previously unreleased information about how the company trains and serves Claude across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, and AMD GPUs. The video features co-founder Tom Brown discussing an unconventional multi-chip strategy that enables training on all four chip families with minimal human intervention.
items.title: Anthropic's IPO Roadshow Video Reveals Multi-Chip Compute Strategy

items.summary: The AI industry is still reeling from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s honeypot scandal, but some see it as larger than one man. Nate Singer of Heron Intelligence says similar cases are common in the semiconductor sector and often stay under the radar. He cites at least three reports plus decades-long Chinese economic espionage targeting executives.
items.title: Nvidia Honypot Scandal Seen as Wider Industry Problem

items.summary: Bloomberg reported, citing anonymous sources, that OpenAI’s quarterly revenue crossed $10 billion for the first time in Q3 2025. If true, this would represent an almost 50% jump from $6.7 billion in sales the company reportedly recorded in the second quarter. The report attributed the increase to strong demand for its recent AI models and noted OpenAI’s annual revenue run rate reached $50 billion.
items.title: OpenAI Quarterly Revenue Crosses $10 Billion for First Time

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Anthropic is rolling out new features for its paid Team and Enterprise plans, including Claude Meetings, a beta Whiteboards feature, Record-a-Skill, Sheets, and Data. The company said the tools let users add Claude to meetings to take notes and update documents live, go beyond transcription by proactively contributing action items, turn spoken ideas into timelines or decks, create shareable spreadsheets with tracked changes, and query external data sources like Amazon Redshift. Anthropic stated Team plans get all three features on by default, while Enterprise admins control access starting Nov. 19, 2025.
items.title: Anthropic Adds Meeting and Spreadsheet Tools for Teams

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted an affair reportedly with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive accused of working with the Chinese government. NVIDIA’s board says it is still investigating and sees no reason to believe trade secrets were compromised. The item then lists ten notable examples, opening with spy dramas like The Americans (2013-2018), Red Sparrow (2018) and Lust, Caution (2007).
items.title: Nvidia CEO's alleged spy affair and Hollywood honey trap films

items.summary: Amazon Web Services describes Tiros, its automated-reasoning tool, as an alternative to dynamic packet sampling for validating network segmentation across all modeled paths. Previously used in customer-facing services such as Amazon Inspector, VPC Reachability Analyzer, and Network Access Analyzer, the approach treats validation as a static process: configurations are converted into logical propositions that tools can analyze. Using Tiros, AWS analyzes topology hourly and provides a mathematical demonstration that the topological description aligns with isolation specifications; if actual reachability matches expected segmentation, the check succeeds, otherwise it alerts an operator. The method applies to Cloud WAN customers configuring organizational networks.
items.title: AWS Offers Tiros for Math-Based Network Segmentation Validation

items.summary: Meta describes Intelligent Delivery, an ML-driven system that allocates compute across its ad-serving stack toward a globally optimal outcome. The article states the approach has delivered roughly 10% incremental ranking performance since 2017 through mid-2026 on major surfaces. It outlines three capabilities: predicting which requests benefit most from extra compute, using layered decision engines to shift traffic and resources across regions, hardware generations and hosts under a latency budget, and an agentic AI loop that contributed about 20% of optimizations in the first half of 2026. Meta frames serving efficiency as increasingly difficult because models grow faster than the hardware can run them.
items.title: Meta Shares Intelligent Delivery System for Allocating Ads Compute

items.summary: Security researchers at Arctic Wolf report attackers are using Alibaba Cloud to host self-managed instances of AntiFox, an open-source agentic penetration-testing platform. In observed intrusions, the infrastructure was linked to confirmed malicious actions against internet-facing web services and associated AWS environments, including deploying an ASPX webshell on an internet-exposed IIS server and harvesting production secrets via valid IAM credentials in about 30 minutes.
items.title: Hackers Abuse AntiFox AI Tool on Alibaba Cloud for AWS Attacks

items.summary: Google is introducing Tabletop, a new Google Labs experiment designed for real-time collaboration among groups planning trips, leagues or gatherings. Users add links, files and ideas, then prompt @tabletop to generate interactive trip itineraries, dinner polls, expense splitters and tournament brackets in one shared space. The tool launches in the U.S. via an 18+ waitlist.
items.title: Google Introduces Tabletop for Group Planning and Play

items.summary: City Developments Limited (CDL) expects significantly weaker financial performance for its second half ending Dec 31, 2026. The group said capital-recycling deals now expected to complete in the 2027 financial year will reduce gains versus H2 2025’s $473.1 million from South Beach Consortium divestment. Weakness is compounded by Korean won appreciation and possible property-portfolio impairment losses.
items.title: CDL Warns of Weaker Second-Half Performance in 2026

items.summary: Google announced a preview of two new SQL functions — ai.classify and ai.extract — available in the google_ml_integration extension (version 1.6.1 or later) on PostgreSQL 18, allowing users to classify text and extract structured JSON directly inside their databases using standard SQL.
items.title: AlloyDB previews in-database AI classification and extraction functions

items.summary: Google Cloud is introducing the Professional Agentic Architect certification as part of its Gemini Agent Ready (GEAR) initiative, marking a shift from prompting to architecting production-ready agents. Nearly one million developers use GEAR for agent training; over four months Google trained thousands of forward-deployed engineers and partners on an internal curriculum now opening to the broader developer community. The exam uses a new hybrid format combining conceptual knowledge with hands-on labs in live cloud environments across five domains, including low-code tools and custom Gemini agents. Ipsos research cited by Google shows 82% of learners say mentioning Google Cloud certifications drives more recruiter responses, while 90% credit credentials for filling in-demand roles. The certification is offered at no cost to registrants.
items.title: Google Cloud Launches Professional Agentic Architect Certification

items.summary: Bright Machines lets customers view live factory dashboards without opening inbound access to its air-gapped plants, capturing PostgreSQL changes at the edge with Debezium and Apache Iceberg. The data travels over a single auditable outbound path before Databricks reads it in place through Unity Catalog federation, enforcing floor-matched role-based permissions. A row committed on the line is queryable within one to two minutes at steady state, while operators keep using real-time on-prem dashboards. Proof of concept took about six weeks with two engineers; the first customer-visible dashboard went live about two months after kickoff.
items.title: Bright Machines Shares Factory Data Without Opening Air-Gapped Plants

items.summary:
In a New Yorker piece dated Nov 11, 2026, Allison Stanger and Bruce Schneier examine how AI companies invoke the First Amendment to dodge accountability. Character. AI argued its chatbot’s words were protected speech and that it was merely a service; Judge Anne Conway rejected both in May 2025. The pattern repeats: OpenAI cited free speech after a teen suicide, xAI claimed Grok outputs are expressive acts even when they praise Hitler, Google defended AI Overviews as summaries of the web, and Air Canada called its chatbot a separate legal entity. Stanger argues that where no human chose the words, no speech right attaches — “Verbiage that no person chose is a product, and the company that built the model should answer for it. ” She calls for federal law making builders liable for machine outputs.

The authors contend AI systems can now produce millions of tailored messages an hour, reversing assumptions about costly speech.
items.title: AI Firms Seek Speech Shield From Liability

items.summary: Beijing collected over US$160 billion in back taxes from its ultra-wealthy on offshore trusts, Xinhua reported. October receipts alone drove nearly a 90% jump in national personal income tax revenue for the month, with most taxpayers cooperating proactively. The haul falls short of Barclays’ worst-case estimate but matches domestic lawyers’ expectations.
items.title: China’s offshore trust tax drive yields $30 billion

items.summary: Karen Crasta wrote in a forum post that the “Stand on either side of the escalator” trial should extend to stations serving passengers with different mobility needs, especially those travelling to hospitals. She cited Kent Ridge MRT station, which serves National University Hospital (NUH) and the National University of Singapore, where she observed congestion between 8.30am and 10am during morning peak.
items.title: Commuter urges extension of escalator trial to Kent Ridge MRT

items.summary: SG Enable’s refreshed Enabling Mark framework took effect Nov 11 and places greater emphasis on sustained employment for persons with disabilities, according to the item. It notes that support must continue when staff around an employee change, suggesting employers treat a supervisor change as a routine checkpoint. SG Enable could pilot a simple checklist within existing handover procedures.
items.title: SG Enable refreshes framework on supporting disabled workers as supervisors change

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Microsoft’s November Patch Tuesday update resolves 1,094 security vulnerabilities, according to Microsoft, with 63 of them rated critical and one already exploited in the wild. The exploited flaw is a spoofing vulnerability in Outlook labeled Moderate but capable of letting an attacker connect the user to their own network without warning and potentially leak NTLMv2 hash credentials. Jack Bicer, Director of Vulnerability Research at patch management provider Action1, said attackers are already exploiting it with just one click on an email file. The update also adds a customizable right-click menu in File Explorer and gradually rolls out Cloud rebuild for Windows recovery.
items.title: Microsoft’s November Patch Fixes Over a Thousand Windows Flaws as One Is Exploited

items.summary: The article introduces pooling-aware training for multi-vector embedding models, which keep several contextual token vectors per document to enable fine-grained query matches. The author trains a model with Sentence Transformers using two averaged losses: one on full embeddings and one after compressing documents by roughly one quarter via HierarchicalTokenPooling's Ward clustering. On NanoBEIR@13, the trained pooling-aware model raises nDCG@10 retention from 94.6% to 97.8%, improving mean score from 49.03 to 51.23 while storing 74.8% fewer document vectors than unpooled retrieval. A straight-through estimator passes gradients through cluster assignments, and a separate baseline trained without pooling retains only 93.3%. The author notes the gains transfer to fixed caps and adaptive thresholds.
items.title: Pooling-Aware Training Improves Multi-Vector Retrieval Compression

items.summary:
A reader praises Alex Pearce for unplugging his fridge from the internet, questioning why he waited until after hacked fridges topped headlines.

The letter argues that many connected devices are vulnerable: their firmware is rarely upgraded, security features are weak, most can run offline, and some already belong to a botnet. AI has shortened the time needed to find exploits. The writer advises upgrading if confident or unplugging otherwise.
items.title: Letter warns of hacked fridges and internet-of-shit dangers

items.summary: The acknowledgements page of AlphaGenome 2, titled 'Deciphering how cells read DNA to better understand disease,' thanks a long list of contributors. It credits Adam Gayoso, Alexander Karollus and others with the core research work, then lists additional people who gave support and feedback.
items.title: AlphaGenome 2 Decodes How Cells Read DNA for Disease Insight

items.summary: The Independent Games Festival jury released a statement declining to vote for any game using generative AI, sparking debate in indie development this week. Big Walk developer House House publicly disclosed that large language models were used sparingly near the end of its co-operative puzzle exploration game “to help work through some difficult technical challenges and bugs,” representing well under 0.1% of the code.
items.title: Indie Studio Discloses Minimal AI Use After Jury Backlash

items.summary: Radical Numerics announced Omnii Defense, an edge model that flags natural and AI-engineered pathogens on a laptop with no internet needed. Its CEO Eric Nguyen compares biodefense to cybersecurity’s arms race. In testing, the tool detected 33 percent of Bundibugyo virus sequences as pathogenic even after removing that species from training data, dropping to 22 percent when its whole genus was removed—far above non-AI tools. Access is limited to vetted testers while national labs and agencies evaluate it.
items.title: Startup Offers AI Tool Against Bioweapons

items.summary: At a Berlin conference, Porsche CEO Michael Leiters said the company wants “to completely steer clear from any kind of effects and shows,” according to Bloomberg. He contrasted Tesla’s mid-air Roadster demonstration with Porsche’s Mission S supercar concept, arguing the two target different customers. Ferrari CEO Benedetto Vigna rated the Roadster launch 10 out of 10 last month. Commenters questioned whether the thruster demo reflects a sellable car, noting its range fell from promised 620 miles in 2017 to “over 300” today.
items.title: Porsche CEO Criticizes Tesla Roadster Stunt Show

items.summary: Vanda Research says Anthropic's Nasdaq debut could draw record retail buying, potentially surpassing SpaceX and reaching about $250 million in net purchases. Global macro strategist Viraj Patel said pre-IPO perpetual futures trading on Hyperliquid suggests a historic retail surge. The firm notes only six stocks have topped that threshold since 2024.
items.title: Vanda Research Forecasts Record Retail Buying for Anthropic IPO

items.summary: Spain's data protection watchdog AEPD said on Wednesday it had launched a probe into alleged child sexual abuse material on TikTok, brought to light by local outlet Maldita.es. However, the agency rejected the government's demand to temporarily block the app in Spain, opting instead for measures targeting specific content involving unlawful treatment of minors' data. The lead European regulator is Ireland's Data Protection Commission.
items.title: Spain's AEPD launches TikTok probe but rejects government block demand

items.summary: The News frames the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as a victory for 'China hawks' in the Trump administration. The company's market value reportedly fell about $280 billion, and it now faces a board probe and lawsuits. Officials allege Megaspeed may be smuggling chips into China via Singapore. Critics like Steve Bannon and Dario Amodei of Anthropic oppose export controls; Reed argues the government should clarify whether an investigation is underway before leaking documents.
items.title: Critics Celebrate Nvidia’s China Export Fallout After Jensen Huang Scandal

items.summary: Reliance Digital advertises the iPhone 17 Pro (256GB) for an effective price of ₹54,990 after a bank discount and exchange bonus on a used iPhone 15 Pro. The deal requires trading in an older phone; without it, the price rises to about ₹89,990.
items.title: Reliance Digital Offers iPhone 17 Pro at ₹54,990 With Bank and Exchange Discounts

items.summary: Noel Tata will retire from the chairman and director roles at Tata Investment Corporation on November 11, 2026. He becomes a non-executive chairman emeritus starting December 12, 2026. Bahram Vakil takes over as new chairman from December 12, 2026.
items.title: Tata Investment Corporation Names New Chairman as Noel Tata Retires

items.summary: Scrutiny intensified over the Trump administration's knowledge of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, a week before a superpower summit. The New York Times reported Trump was told in May that Washington had intelligence of the affair; Axios said his commerce secretary received a warning memo. Commerce reportedly delays blacklisting the company accused of smuggling advanced chips to China.
items.title: White House scrutiny intensifies over Nvidia CEO's affair

items.summary: South Africa notified the launch of a safeguard investigation into certain non-wired float glass products, per its notification available in G/SG/N/6/ZAF/15. Interested parties must make themselves known and submit written information within 20 days after initiation; requests for hearings go to the Directorate: Trade Remedies II at The DTI Campus, Sunnyside Pretoria. A safeguard investigation determines whether increased imports cause or threaten serious injury to a domestic industry.
items.title: South Africa Launches Float Glass Safeguard Investigation

items.summary: Labour MPs warn against weakening the UK’s electric vehicle target, which requires 80% of cars sold by 2030 to be electric. As divided cabinet ministers prepare for a Thursday meeting on whether to change it, caucus chair Chris Hinchliff and members argue cuts would undermine net zero ambitions and credibility. Business secretary Jonathan Reynolds wants 50%, transport secretary Heidi Alexander about 60%, while energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh favours keeping it near 80%.
items.title: Labour MPs Urge Government Not To Weaken Electric Vehicle Targets

items.summary: For 25 years the Esecaflor Project in Pará subjected roughly one hectare of Caxiuanã National Forest to artificial drought, diverting about 50% of rainwater. After two decades with half normal rainfall, large trees died and biomass fell by nearly 50%, yet smaller trees redistributed water so mortality reversed and the forest reached a new equilibrium rather than collapsing into savanna. Lead researcher Lucy Rowland warns it will never become savanna but instead a novel degraded ecosystem, cautioning against that term’s negative connotation. The team argues the rainforest adjusts to long-term drought.
items.title: A Dried Amazon Reached a New Equilibrium Rather Than Becoming Savanna

items.summary: Finland has approved Tesla's assisted driving technology, allowing it to be used on Finnish roads after the company made changes. The Transport and Communications Agency (Traficom) announced that Tesla can immediately offer the system in Finland. This comes as Europe faces regulatory challenges over automated driving rules.
items.title: Finland Approves Tesla Assisted Driving Ahead of EU Vote

items.summary: After declaring victory over absolute poverty in 2020, China frames preventing relapse as an ongoing challenge requiring continuous monitoring and oversight reaching down to the grassroots. Officials seek early signs of hardship so local authorities respond quickly with targeted assistance. The article illustrates this through a Hunan village where warnings and support help vulnerable families stay out of poverty.
items.title: China's Grassroots Efforts to Prevent Poverty Relapse

items.summary: In Eastern China's Zhejiang Province, officials must present a digital code before inspecting businesses, allowing companies to verify the inspector and report irregularities. This system exemplifies how the CPC seeks accountability through collaboration with government departments overseeing law enforcement.
items.title: China Tests Digital Codes for Business Inspections in Zhejiang

items.summary: President Trump praised defense secretary Pete Hegseth a day after Republicans killed an impeachment effort, while also defending the Iran war as necessary. Separately, the US may lose its measles elimination status amid a 35-year-worst outbreak of more than 5,400 cases.
items.title: Trump backs Hegseth amid impeachment failure and measles warning

items.summary: Moscow's foreign ministry announced Wednesday that Alexander Darchiev, Russia's ambassador to the United States, died suddenly aged 66 after about one and a half years in office. The ministry praised him as an outstanding diplomat, experienced leader and kind colleague but gave no further details on his death.
items.title: Russia's Ambassador Darchiev Dies at 66

items.summary: Senegalese breakdancers practiced in Dakar ahead of the country's hosting of the Youth Olympic Games this month, marking the first time an Olympic event is held on African soil. Coach Francis Siméon Gomis said their routines mix traditional dances like mbalax and Yela with American and European influence. Suzanne Toure, 15 years old, is the only girl on the national team.
items.title: Senegal Breakdancers Prepare for Youth Olympics

items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was moved from his Washington DC home to a military base after Iran-linked threats, according to US media reports. CBS said the relocation followed a Wall Street Journal photo that exposed his Georgetown address. A source told CBS security concerns prompted authorities to relocate him. The Treasury Department stated he remains committed to pressuring Iran's economy.
items.title: Treasury Secretary Bessent Relocated After Alleged Iranian Threats

items.summary: Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka submitted his resignation, an aide told the BBC, after the Supreme Court ruled a high-school document from his 2024 campaign invalid. The move may strain Prabowo Subianto and Joko Widodo's ruling alliance amid personnel reshuffles, cabinet resignations and student protests over corruption and wildfires.
items.title: Indonesian Vice-President Resigns Amid Alliance Tensions

items.summary: CGTN presents a new documentary titled "The Sea We Call Home," offering five stories of people living with the sea across islands and fishing communities. It follows fishermen and their families whose lives are shaped by finding fresh water, navigating inherited routes, diving reefs, exploring fishing grounds, and waiting for boats to return.
items.title: CGTN Documentary Explores Life Along South China Sea Communities

items.summary: A gallery called The Sea We Call Home presents eight pictures capturing the beauty of the South China Sea and its islands, which people call home. Described as reefs, islands and blue waters stretching to the horizon, the collection frames these places picture by picture.
items.title: Gallery Captures Beauty of South China Sea Islands

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India issued the Domestic Money Transfer Directions, 2026, allowing walk-in customers to remit funds up to ₹50,000 via NEFT. Banks may also permit transfers through Business Correspondents and ATMs capped at ₹5,000 per transaction with a monthly limit of ₹25,000. Cash pay-outs are limited to ₹10,000 per transaction and ₹25,000 monthly per beneficiary. The Reserve Bank said fund transfers would occur on a real-time or near real-time basis.
items.title: RBI Sets Domestic Money Transfer Limits for Walk-in Customers

items.summary: Scale AI co-founder Lucy Guo has filed a federal court request for records from Meta as she prepares a potential UK defamation case against former girlfriend Wallis Day. The subpoena, reported by The San Francisco Standard on November 3, seeks details of an Instagram Story posted in May about viewership and reach. Guo described the posts as “replete with falsehoods”.
items.title: Lucy Guo Seeks Instagram Story Data in Defamation Dispute

items.summary: Anthropic is expanding its use of AI in drug discovery, partnering with six organisations including Generate Biomedicines and BigHat Biosciences to explore new medicines. One project shortened therapy genetic instructions by about 70 per cent while boosting immune responses; another tested around 1,010 variations for a cancer-targeting candidate. Work also generated roughly 35,000 antibody designs in about a month. The company cautioned that most research remains preclinical and has not reached human trials.
items.title: Anthropic CEO Promises Cancer Cure Within a Decade

items.summary: OpenAI’s CFO Sarah Friar said the company will keep investing in AI data centres despite voter opposition during the US midterm elections. She linked continued spending to customer demand and outlined efforts to build community trust, following a policy blueprint published before her interview. OpenAI also plans a potential stock market debut in 2027 and continues fundraising, with an initial $11 billion round closed and up to another $9 billion possible.
items.title: OpenAI CFO Vows Continued Data Centre Investment Amid Voter Pushback

items.summary: Republican Senator Cramer called for Jensen Huang's resignation, citing a possible foreign intelligence effort targeting NVIDIA. The company launched an independent investigation on November 8 and said it has no reason to believe national security or secrets were compromised. Under Section 29(a) and Section 32 of its bylaws, the board may remove officers at any time with or without cause.
items.title: NVIDIA bylaws let board remove Huang; senator urges his exit

items.summary: Amazon's Ring launched two autonomous security products on Tuesday, a flying indoor camera for homes and a roving robot for businesses, expanding beyond its home-security lineup. Both use the AI Pilot system to map spaces and navigate obstacles. The Ring Rover Cam ships December 16 at $999.99 in the US; the Ring Drone Cam arrives January 27 at $249.99.
items.title: Amazon's Ring Launches Autonomous Flying and Roving Security Robots

items.summary: Christopher Cooter, Canada's high commissioner to India, says Ottawa is confident of finalising the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's December 11-12 visit. He noted ratification would still take time because provincial governments are involved, and that the agreement must be ratified on both sides before it becomes legal. Cooter described progress as far beyond a reset since Mark Carney took office, following ties that nosedived in 2023 after Canada alleged Indian state involvement in Hardeep Singh Nijjar's killing. He also addressed student-policy concerns and said the relationship is now built on deep economic linkages.
items.title: Canada envoy sees trade breakthrough before Modi visit

items.summary: Anthropic announced Tuesday it is bringing its Claude assistant into video conference platform Google Meet as a visible participant, letting users add Claude to calls where it follows the conversation and turns discussions into work in real time. The feature launches in beta for Team and Enterprise customers initially through Google Meet, part of Anthropic's push toward an initial public offering with plans to raise up to $64.4 billion at a $1.02 trillion valuation.
items.title: Anthropic Adds Claude Assistant to Google Meet Video Calls

items.summary: Two Special Police Officers went missing from Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar district on Wednesday, prompting a search operation. Both were part of the Special Operations Group deployed near Dachhan. The incident coincided with an attack at a security checkpoint in Kulgam, where three Central Reserve Police Force personnel were injured after unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire around 2.15 pm; two sustained minor injuries and one was slightly serious before being shifted to Government Medical College Anantnag.
items.title: Two SPOs Missing in J&K Kishtwar as CRPF Checkpoint Attacked

items.summary: Stock market analysis by ACE Equity shows that 769 stocks declined between October 8 and November 8, even as the benchmark Nifty climbed 2,812 points or 12.65% over the same period. The divergence reflects buying concentrated in heavyweight large-cap companies while smaller stocks continued to struggle. Apurva Sheth of SAMCO Securities attributes the gap partly to valuation: several largecaps had fallen sharply during a correction beginning January 2026, making them more attractive as crude oil prices eased. Foreign institutional investors returned strongly, reportedly buying $4.1 billion worth of Indian equities in November alone, according to Reuters, favouring liquid names such as ICICI Bank and Reliance Industries.
items.title: Why Smallcaps Fell as Nifty Rose Amid Foreign Buying

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India said banks can offer cash pay-out and pay-in services under its revised Domestic Money Transfer (DMT) Directions, 2026. The RBI said the maximum amount that can be transferred under the Cash Payout is ₹10,000 per transaction with a monthly ceiling of ₹25,000 per beneficiary. For cash pay-in service, a walk-in customer at a bank branch can remit up to ₹50,000 through NEFT and transfer funds via Business Correspondents or ATMs up to ₹5,000 per transaction with a monthly cap of ₹25,000 per remitter.
items.title: RBI Allows Banks To Offer Cash Pay-In And Pay-Out Under Revised Money Transfer Rules
